question: During a total abdominal hysterectomy, at which anatomical location is the ureter most at risk of inadvertent injury?

answers.text: As it crosses over the pelvic brim at the bifurcation of the common iliac artery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The ureter does cross the pelvic brim near the common iliac bifurcation, but injury at this level is uncommon in standard hysterectomy — the surgical field is above the major dissection planes.

answers.text: As it passes under the uterine artery ('water flows under the bridge')

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The ureter passes approximately 1.5 cm lateral to the cervix and runs under the uterine artery at the level of the internal os — the classic 'water under the bridge' relationship. This is the single most important ureteric danger zone in hysterectomy.

answers.text: At the infundibulopelvic ligament during ligation of the ovarian vessels

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The ureter does lie medial to the IP ligament and can be injured there, particularly during oophorectomy, but the primary danger zone in hysterectomy is the ureter-uterine artery crossing near the cervix.

answers.text: As it enters the bladder trigone posteriorly

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: By the time the ureter reaches the trigone it is well protected by the bladder wall. Injuries at the trigone level are rare in standard hysterectomy compared with the uterine artery crossing zone.

overallFeedback.feedback: The most important anatomical relationship in hysterectomy is the ureter running under the uterine artery near the internal cervical os. Commit the 'water under the bridge' mnemonic to memory.
Correct. The ureter passes under the uterine artery about 1.5 cm lateral to the cervix — 'water flows under the bridge' is the mnemonic every student must know before observing a hysterectomy.
